page.title: Virtual Summit Platforms: How to Choose and What to Prepare
page.description: A practical guide to picking a virtual summit platform, matching cost models, staffing production roles, and proving backup readiness before you sign.
page.h1: What should you decide first about virtual summit platforms?
page.definition: Virtual summit platforms are software suites that host multi-session online events with registration, networking, and analytics, distinct from single-session webinar tools and from the production crew that runs the show.
page.quick_answer: Lock the audience outcome and session format first, then match a cost model to your buying process, and confirm you have the production roles and backup stream covered before you commit.

sections.h2: What audience outcome and format must you settle before choosing a platform?

blocks.p: The platform must support the specific attendee journey you promise, whether that is a single-track keynote series, concurrent breakouts with live Q&A, or an expo hall with sponsored booths.

ul: Define the primary outcome: lead generation, community building, product education, or revenue from tickets.
Map the session types: keynotes, panels, workshops, roundtables, office hours, and sponsor demos.
Decide on networking mechanics: one-to-one matching, topic tables, or open chat channels.
Confirm accessibility needs: live captions, sign language windows, and downloadable transcripts.
Set the replay strategy: gated on-demand library, public YouTube playlist, or drip-fed email series.

sections.h2: How many platforms should you compare and what categories exist?

blocks.p: Ten platforms compared below, from self-serve streaming studios to enterprise event suites, cluster into four categories that map to the format decisions you made earlier.

ul: Streaming studios: StreamYard, Restream, Riverside — browser-based, producer-friendly, limited attendee interaction.
Webinar-first suites: Zoom Webinars, Livestorm, GoToWebinar — built for registration, Q&A, polls, and CRM sync.
Virtual event platforms: Hopin, Goldcast, Airmeet, vFairs — multi-stage, networking, expo, gamification, analytics.
Enterprise event clouds: ON24, Cvent, Bizzabo — deep Marketo, Salesforce, and Eloqua integration, compliance tooling, dedicated success managers.

sections.h2: What production roles does a summit need that a webinar does not?

blocks.p: A summit needs six to eight weeks of management; a webinar three to four, and the staffing gap widens with each concurrent track.

ol: Show caller — owns the run of show, cues every transition, and holds the backup stream trigger.
Speaker manager — coordinates green-room checks, slide uploads, and rehearsal scheduling for every presenter.
Moderator — monitors live chat, curates audience questions, and feeds them to speakers on cue.
Platform operator — drives the broadcast software, manages screen shares, lower thirds, and recording starts and stops.
Technical director — oversees encoder health, redundant internet paths, and the failover stream to a secondary CDN.

sections.h2: What backup-path readiness proves the platform choice is solid?

blocks.p: The platform is not the production; someone still has to own the run of show, rehearse speakers and keep a backup stream ready.

ul: Run one full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before, and a technical check sixty minutes before going live.
Configure a simultaneous backup stream to a second CDN or to a private YouTube unlisted link.
Prepare a static holding page with a countdown timer and a fallback embed code if the primary player fails.
Assign the show caller a single hotkey or chat command that switches the audience to the backup without speaker involvement.
Document the failover decision tree in the run of show so every role knows the trigger, the action, and the communication script.

faq.q: Can I run a summit on the webinar licence I already own?
faq.a: Yes, if your format is single-track with under five hundred attendees and you accept limited networking. Multi-track agendas, virtual expo booths, and advanced analytics usually require a virtual event platform tier.

faq.q: How far in advance should I lock the platform contract?
faq.a: Plan a hybrid conference six to eight weeks out; lock the venue AV and the platform before the agenda is final. For pure virtual summits, allow two to three weeks from brief to live; a repeat format can move faster.

faq.q: What deliverables should I expect from a production partner?
faq.a: Deliverables include run of show, speaker brief and rehearsal, branded slide template and lower thirds, live producer, Q&A moderation, backup stream, edited recording and clips. West Peek Productions produces virtual, hybrid and webinar events and sets up marketing, content and creative operations.

faq.q: When should the replay be available to attendees?
faq.a: Send the replay within twenty-four to forty-eight hours, while attendees still remember the event. Host it on the same platform or move it to a gated library with chapter markers for each session.

faq.q: Do I need a dedicated platform operator if I use a streaming studio?
faq.a: A single producer can run a simple webinar on StreamYard or Riverside, but summits with concurrent stages need a platform operator separate from the show caller to manage scene changes, screen shares, and recording controls without missing cues.
